rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~50-100 cSt / ~2.5wt) at a time. Thicker rear oil holds the chassis flatter on power and gives pack for landings; too thick kills forward bite over bumps.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.39 (Shock Fluid — thicker/heavier oil: less bottoming out; off-road)
Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide (rear 60wt: ample pack for jump landings, keeps chassis roll to a minimum)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Oil (corroboration: heavier oil better for smooth tracks, decreases responsiveness)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~50-100 cSt) thinner at a time. Frees the rear to react over bumps for forward bite on rough/loose surfaces; too thin lets the rear roll and wallow.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.39 (Shock Fluid — thinner/lighter oil: faster rebound for many small bumps; off-road)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Oil (corroboration: lighter oil more responsive, better for bumpy conditions, allows more chassis roll)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~50-100 cSt) at a time. Slows the front to calm dive into jumps and braking twitch; too thick makes the front skate over bumps and steering go lazy.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.39 (Shock Fluid — thicker/heavier oil: less bottoming out; off-road)
Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide (front lighter than rear to balance the lighter front end; thicker oil keeps chassis from bottoming harshly)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Oil (corroboration: heavier oil seems sluggish, better for smooth tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~50-100 cSt) thinner at a time. Frees the front to follow rough ground and react quicker on turn-in; too thin lets the front dive on braking and off jumps.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.39 (Shock Fluid — thinner/lighter oil: faster rebound for many small bumps; off-road)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Oil (corroboration: lighter oil more responsive, better for bumpy conditions)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One piston step (one extra/larger hole) at a time. More holes free the rear over bumps for forward bite; pair with the right oil — pistons set the high/low-speed split, oil sets overall rate.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.40 (Shock Pistons — larger holes: less damping, for small bumps; off-road)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Oil/Pistons (corroboration: more/larger holes pass oil quicker = more responsive damping; rougher track = more holes)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One piston step (one fewer/smaller hole) at a time. Fewer holes add pack so the rear holds up on big landings; too few and it deflects over chop.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.40 (Shock Pistons — smaller holes: more damping/more pack, improve jump lifts and landings for smoother tracks; off-road)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Oil/Pistons (corroboration: fewer/smaller holes pass oil slower; smoother track = fewer holes)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate softer at a time. A softer rear lets the rear squat and load the tyres for forward bite on low grip; on high-bite surfaces it brings on traction roll.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.41 (Shock Springs — softer/lighter tension: great on rear for off-road, gives more traction, best for small bumps)
Dave B Stevens — Essential Off-road RC Racer's Guide (springs) [section TBD]
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Springs (corroboration: softer end gains grip)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate stiffer at a time. A stiffer rear cuts roll and traction-roll on high bite; too stiff and it loses forward bite on low grip.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.41 (Shock Springs — stiffer/heavier tension: creates less traction, lifts higher off jumps, better suspension response)
Dave B Stevens — Essential Off-road RC Racer's Guide (springs) [section TBD]
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Springs (corroboration: stiffer end loses grip / reduces roll)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate softer at a time. A softer front loads the front tyres for more steering and bump compliance; too soft and it dives and traction-rolls on bite.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.41 (Shock Springs — softer/lighter tension: gives more traction, best for small bumps; controls how the car corners)
Dave B Stevens — Essential Off-road RC Racer's Guide (springs) [section TBD]
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Springs (corroboration: heavier springs normally run front than rear; softer end gains grip)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate stiffer at a time. A stiffer front cuts roll and dive and calms a darty front on high bite; too stiff and the front pushes.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.41 (Shock Springs — stiffer/heavier tension: creates less traction, better suspension response, reduces chassis roll)
Dave B Stevens — Essential Off-road RC Racer's Guide (springs) [section TBD]
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Springs (corroboration: stiffer end reduces roll, loses grip)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5deg more negative at a time (typical -1 to -2deg front). Loads the outer front tyre through the corner for more cornering grip; past ~-2deg the straight gets nervous and forward roll grip drops.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.12 (Camber, front — more negative (2 deg.): more high-speed traction through turns; less: more straight-line acceleration)
Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide (front -2.0deg gives a good contact patch through the corner)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Camber (corroboration: more front camber = more aggressive steering, more high-speed cornering traction, less stable on the straight)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5deg more negative at a time (typical -2 to -2.5deg rear). More rear camber adds mid-corner rear grip when it grips and rolls; it costs straight-line forward traction, so don't chase it on loose dirt.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.15 (Camber, rear — more negative (-2 deg.): more high-speed traction through corners; more positive removes straight-line acceleration)
Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide (rear -2.5deg, set by how much rear traction the track needs)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Camber (corroboration: more rear camber = more high-speed cornering traction, less forward traction, less stable on the straight)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5deg toward 0 at a time; never go positive. Standing the rear tyres up puts more flat patch down for forward bite and acceleration; too little and mid-corner rear grip drops.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.15 (Camber, rear — less negative / toward zero: more straight-line acceleration; tyre stands vertical)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Camber (corroboration: less rear camber = more straight-line acceleration, less traction in the corners)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One caster step (~2-3deg) at a time. NOTE on a 2WD buggy kick-up adds to total caster — count both. More caster steadies the straight and adds on-power/exit steering at the cost of initial bite.
sources: Hudy Setup Tips p.18 (Caster, Effects of Caster Adjustment — more caster angle (more inclined): increases straight-line stability, decreases off-power steering at corner entry, makes the car more stable through bumpy track conditions)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Caster (corroboration: more caster = more on-power steering exiting, more stable on straights and through bumps, easier to drive; kick-up adds to total caster in 2WD)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One caster step (~2-3deg) at a time. Less caster sharpens off-power turn-in for tight smooth tracks; it costs straight-line and bump stability, so avoid it on rough/loose tracks.
sources: Hudy Setup Tips p.18 (Caster, Effects of Caster Adjustment — less caster angle (more vertical): decreases straight-line stability, increases off-power steering at corner entry, increases suspension efficiency)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Caster (corroboration: less caster = quicker steering, more off-power steering entering, less stable on straights and through bumps)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5deg toward toe-out at a time, both sides equal (typical 1-3deg total toe-out front on a 2WD). Sharpens initial and off-power turn-in; too much makes the front nervous and grabby.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.49 (Toe-in, toe-out, front — toe-out: quicker corner turn-in; unstable in bumps and slippery on the straightaway)
Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide (toe-out increases instant steering response; base 1.0deg toe-out per side)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Toe (corroboration: toe-out = more off-power steering, more initial turn-in)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5deg toward toe-in at a time, both sides. Calms a nervous front and adds on-power/exit steering and straight-line stability; too much dulls initial turn-in.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.49 (Toe-in, toe-out, front — toe-out is unstable in bumps and on the straightaway, so toe-in / less toe-out is the more stable / straight-line setting); Hudy Setup Tips p.20 (Toe, Effects of Toe Adjustment, front — increasing toe-in: makes car easier to drive; decreasing toe-in: less stable under acceleration)
Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide (toe-in = better straight-line stability and more steering through and out of a corner)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Toe (corroboration: front toe-in = more on-power steering)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5deg more toe-in at a time (typical 2.5-3.5deg total); rear NEVER runs toe-out. Adds forward bite and on-power stability for low grip; costs rotation and a little top speed.
sources: Hudy Setup Tips p.20 (Toe, Effects of Toe Adjustment, rear toe — increasing (more toe-in): more stable exiting on-power at corner exit and braking, less chance of losing rear traction, increases understeer, decreases top speed)
Dave B Stevens — Essential Off-road RC Racer's Guide (rear toe) [section TBD]
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Toe (corroboration: more rear toe-in = more forward traction, slower acceleration, less rotation; best for low-traction tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5deg less toe-in at a time; never reach toe-out. Frees rotation and acceleration on high bite; costs on-power stability — back off on low grip.
sources: Hudy Setup Tips p.20 (Toe, Effects of Toe Adjustment, rear toe — decreasing (less toe-in): less stable at on-power corner exit and braking, more chance of losing rear traction, increases top speed)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Toe (corroboration: less rear toe-in = more high-speed stability, faster acceleration, more rotation; for high-traction surfaces)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1mm at a time via preload, keep front/rear rake intact. Lowers CG for less roll and traction-roll on smooth high-bite; too low and it bottoms and skates on bumps.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.29 (Ride Height, front — lower: less chance of flipping in corners / on carpet; Hudy Setup Tips p.12 (Ride Height, Effects of Ride Height Adjustment): decreasing ride height = increases overall stability)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Ride Height (corroboration: lower = less chassis roll, more responsive, worse for bumps/jumps)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1mm at a time via preload. Raises clearance for rough/rutted/loose tracks; too high adds roll and dulls response, so don't over-raise on smooth high-bite.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.30 (Ride Height, rear — higher: better acceleration in loose terrain, better lift off jumps) + p.29 (Ride Height, front — higher: more chassis roll and better traction on bumpy tracks)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Ride Height (corroboration: higher = more chassis roll, less responsive, better in bumps and jumps)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5-1mm more front down-travel at a time, identical L/R. More front droop lets the front extend and shift weight rearward on power for on-power steering and bump grip; it softens initial steering and high-speed stability.
sources: Hudy Setup Tips p.10 (Downstops, Effects of Downstop Adjustment, Front Downstops — lower downstop value / more front droop: increases upward chassis travel on-throttle, more rearward weight transfer, increases rear traction on corner exit, better on bumpy tracks)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Droop (corroboration: more front droop = more weight transfer to rear accelerating, more on-power steering, less aggressive steering, less stable at high speed)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5-1mm less front down-travel at a time, identical L/R. Less front droop keeps the front flat for sharper initial steering and high-speed/traction-roll stability; it costs on-power steering.
sources: Hudy Setup Tips p.10 (Downstops, Effects of Downstop Adjustment, Front Downstops — higher downstop value / less front droop: decreases front chassis upward travel on-throttle, less rearward weight transfer, better on smooth tracks, more on-power steering, more responsive in direction change)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Droop (corroboration: less front droop = more aggressive steering, less traction rolling, more stable at high speeds, less on-power steering)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5-1mm more rear down-travel at a time, identical L/R. More rear droop lets the rear extend to find grip over bumps for forward bite; it reduces braking stability.
sources: Hudy Setup Tips p.10 (Downstops, Effects of Downstop Adjustment, Rear Downstops — lower downstop value / more rear droop: increases rear chassis upward travel off-throttle or under braking, less stable under braking, increases steering on corner entry, more turn-in, better on bumpy tracks)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Droop (corroboration: more rear droop = more stable over bumps, more weight transfer to front under braking, less stable under braking)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5-1mm less rear down-travel at a time, identical L/R. Less rear droop keeps the rear flat for braking stability and flatter jumping; it costs rear traction over rough ground.
sources: Hudy Setup Tips p.10 (Downstops, Effects of Downstop Adjustment, Rear Downstops — higher downstop value / less rear droop: decreases rear chassis upward travel off-throttle or under braking, less forward weight transfer, better on smooth tracks; lower value is the one the book calls less stable under braking, so less droop = more braking stability)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Droop (corroboration: less rear droop = more stable under braking, less stable over bumps)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One insert/step (~1deg) at a time, both sides. More anti-squat plants the rear for forward bite on smooth grippy tracks; it reduces on-power steering and can lift the rear on jumps and unsettle bumpy on-power sections.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.8 (Anti-squat, off-road — more anti-squat: less side traction in corners, more rear lift in jumps)
Dave B Stevens — Essential Off-road RC Racer's Guide (anti-squat) [section TBD]
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Anti-Squat (corroboration: more anti-squat = more forward traction, less squat on accel, reduces on-power steering, increases rear wheel lift on jumps)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One insert/step (~1deg) at a time, both sides. Less anti-squat frees on-power steering and side bite and smooths bumpy/slick on-power sections; it trades away some straight-line forward bite.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.8 (Anti-squat, off-road — less anti-squat: more side traction in corners, more rear traction for slick or bumpy surfaces)
Dave B Stevens — Essential Off-road RC Racer's Guide (anti-squat) [section TBD]
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Anti-Squat (corroboration: less anti-squat = more on-power steering, more side traction, more rear traction for slick or bumpy surfaces)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wire size (~0.1mm) thicker at a time, only if the chassis has a rear bar mount (refuse otherwise and fall back to rear spring/shock position). Cuts rear roll and traction-roll and adds rotation on high bite; it costs rear side traction, so avoid on loose dirt.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.7 (Anti-roll Bars, Sway Bars — stiffer/thicker bars for high-traction tracks: minimize chassis roll, more responsive in cornering)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Anti-Roll Bar (corroboration: thicker rear bar = more on-power steering, less chassis roll, more responsive, for high-traction tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wire size (~0.1mm) thinner at a time (or remove the bar). Adds rear roll and side traction for low-grip/rough tracks; on high bite it can bring on traction roll.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.7 (Anti-roll Bars, Sway Bars — softer/thinner bars for low and medium bite tracks: more chassis roll, less responsive)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Anti-Roll Bar (corroboration: thinner rear bar = more chassis roll, less responsive, for low-medium traction tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wire size (~0.1mm) thicker at a time, only if a front bar mount exists (refuse otherwise, fall back to front spring). Cuts front roll and traction-roll on high bite; on low grip/loose dirt it pushes.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.7 (Anti-roll Bars, Sway Bars — stiffer/thicker bars for high-traction tracks minimize chassis roll; a thicker front bar reduces oversteer per the same page)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Anti-Roll Bar (corroboration: thicker front bar = more off-power steering, less chassis roll, more responsive, for high-traction tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wire size (~0.1mm) thinner at a time (or remove). Adds front roll and front grip for low-grip/rough tracks; on high bite it can bring on front traction roll.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.7 (Anti-roll Bars, Sway Bars — softer/thinner bars for low and medium bite tracks: more chassis roll/front grip, less responsive)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Anti-Roll Bar (corroboration: thinner front bar = more chassis roll, less responsive, for low-medium traction tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1/8 turn tighter at a time; set just past slip under hard load. A tighter ball diff drives harder out of corners on grip; on loose/slick tracks a freer diff puts power down more smoothly, so don't over-tighten there.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.21 (Diff Fluid, Rear Diff, off-road — thicker/heavier (tighter-coupling analog): less grip but more stability on power, for high-traction conditions)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Differential (corroboration: tighter diff = more instant throttle response and greater acceleration; looser diff for low-traction tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1/8 turn looser at a time; never so loose it slips under normal throttle. A freer diff lets the inside rear differentiate for smoother power-down and rotation on slick/loose tracks; it costs direct drive on high bite.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.21 (Diff Fluid, Rear Diff, off-road — thinner/lighter (looser-coupling analog): more grip but less stability on power, for low-traction conditions)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Differential (corroboration: looser diff for low-traction tracks; tighter = more instant response)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1/8 turn looser at a time. A looser slipper cushions the power hit so the rear tyres hook up instead of spinning on low grip, and protects the drivetrain on jumps; too loose wastes acceleration and overheats.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.43 (Slipper Clutch — looser for tracks with low traction: more traction exiting corner)
Dave B Stevens — Essential Off-road RC Racer's Guide (slipper clutch) [section TBD]

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1/8 turn tighter at a time. A tighter slipper delivers more direct drive on high bite; on low grip it lets the rear spin up, so loosen rather than tighten on loose/slick tracks.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.43 (Slipper Clutch — tighter for high-bite tracks: more instant acceleration, smoother corner entry)
Dave B Stevens — Essential Off-road RC Racer's Guide (slipper clutch) [section TBD]

rules.magnitude_guidance: Step one compound softer (or change tread to match the surface). Softer rears add forward bite on low-bite/cold/loose surfaces but overheat and wear fast on high bite/hot — match compound to surface and temperature first.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.45 (Tyre Compound — softer compound for smoother surfaces; selecting a softer compound to find grip)
Dave B Stevens — Essential Off-road RC Racer's Guide (28 pages on tyres) [section TBD]

rules.magnitude_guidance: Step one compound harder. On high-bite/hot/abrasive surfaces a harder rear stays cooler and keeps consistent grip where a soft tyre would grease over; useless on cold/loose tracks.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.45 (Tyre Compound — harder compound for bumpier surfaces, for grass and higher-wear conditions; stays consistent where a soft tyre would grease over)
Dave B Stevens — Essential Off-road RC Racer's Guide (28 pages on tyres) [section TBD]

rules.magnitude_guidance: Step one insert firmer. A firmer rear insert holds the carcass up under load to resist traction roll and fold on high bite; on rough/loose ground it stops the tyre conforming and loses grip.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.46 (Tyre Inserts, foam — harder insert: less rolling resistance, better cornering; too firm causes bounce / loss of traction)
Dave B Stevens — Essential Off-road RC Racer's Guide (tyres / inserts) [section TBD]

rules.magnitude_guidance: Step one insert softer. A softer rear insert lets the tyre wrap rough/loose ground for mechanical grip; on high bite it folds under load and traction-rolls.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.46 (Tyre Inserts, foam — softer insert: more traction, more drag; lets the tyre conform to the surface)
Dave B Stevens — Essential Off-road RC Racer's Guide (tyres / inserts) [section TBD]

rules.magnitude_guidance: One pinion tooth at a time, then check motor temp after a run (target ~well under the motor's limit). Taller gearing adds top speed on long straights but pulls harder on the motor — back off if it runs hot.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.28 (Pinion Gear — more teeth: more top speed, less run time, gear ratio goes up)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — gearing (corroboration: more pinion = more top speed, less acceleration, more heat)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One pinion tooth at a time. Shorter gearing adds punch off slow corners on tight tracks and runs cooler; it tops out earlier, so don't over-gear-down for long straights.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets p.28 (Pinion Gear — fewer teeth: more acceleration, more run time, gear ratio goes down)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — gearing (corroboration: fewer pinion teeth = more acceleration, less top speed, cooler)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~few thousand cSt, or the next labelled grade) thicker at a time. A thicker front diff tightens the driven front to calm entry and add mid-corner front traction and on-power stability; too thick and the front pushes on entry.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.19 Diff Fluid, Front Diff, off-road (thicker = less steering but more stability on power, for high-traction conditions)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Differential (corroboration: thicker front diff oil reduces corner-entry steering, adds mid-corner stability)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step thinner at a time. A thinner front diff frees the driven front to differentiate for sharper corner-entry steering on low grip — the first lever against 4WD push; too thin makes the car darty and unstable on entry.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.19 Diff Fluid, Front Diff, off-road (thinner = more steering but less stability, for low-traction conditions)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Differential (corroboration: thinner front diff oil frees entry steering on low grip)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~5-10k cSt) thicker at a time. A thicker centre diff locks front-to-rear for harder drive off the corner on grip; it costs steering and adds push and gets worse in bumps, so don't chase it on loose/rough tracks.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.18 Diff Fluid, Centre Diff, off-road (thicker = accelerates harder but worse in bumps, for smooth high-traction conditions)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Centre Differential (corroboration: thicker centre oil adds drive and push, reduces steering)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step thinner at a time. A thinner centre diff frees rotation and steering and smooths acceleration over bumps for low-grip/rough tracks; too thin and the car loses drive off the corner on grip.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.18 Diff Fluid, Centre Diff, off-road (thinner = smoother acceleration, better in bumps, for rough low-traction conditions)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Centre Differential (corroboration: thinner centre oil frees steering and rotation)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~1-2k cSt) thicker at a time. A thicker rear diff smooths power delivery and adds on-power stability so the rear stops stepping out; too thick and the car won't rotate and pushes.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.21 Diff Fluid, Rear Diff, off-road (thicker = less grip but more stability on power, for high-traction conditions)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Differential (corroboration: thicker rear diff oil smooths power, adds stability, reduces rotation)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step thinner at a time. A thinner rear diff lets the inside rear differentiate for more mechanical grip and rotation on low grip; too thin and the rear gets loose and unstable on power on high bite.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.21 Diff Fluid, Rear Diff, off-road (thinner = more grip but less stability on power, for low-traction conditions)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Differential (corroboration: thinner rear diff oil adds rear grip and rotation on low grip)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~50-100 cSt / ~2.5wt) at a time, identical L/R. A heavier front slows dive into jumps and braking and resists bottoming; too thick makes the front skate over bumps and steering go lazy.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.39 Shock Fluid (thicker/heavier = less bottoming out)
petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.1 Damping (Heavier Front: turn radius wider but smoother, the car doesn't hook suddenly, easier to drive)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Oil (corroboration: heavier oil less responsive, better for smooth tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~50-100 cSt) thinner at a time. A lighter front follows rough ground and reacts quicker on turn-in for low-speed steering; too thin lets the front dive on braking and off jumps.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.39 Shock Fluid (thinner/lighter = faster rebound, for many small bumps)
petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.1 Damping (Softer Front: steering reacts quicker, more and better low-speed steering)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Oil (corroboration: lighter oil more responsive, better for bumps)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~50-100 cSt) at a time. A heavier rear holds the chassis flatter on power and gives pack for landings; too thick kills forward bite and traction over bumps.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.39 Shock Fluid (thicker = less bottoming out)
petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.1 Damping (Heavier: more stable, handles smoothly, jumps and lands better)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Oil (corroboration: heavier oil for smooth tracks, decreases responsiveness)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~50-100 cSt) thinner at a time. A lighter rear reacts over bumps for forward bite and traction on rough/loose ground; too thin lets the rear roll and wallow and bottom on landings.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.39 Shock Fluid (thinner/lighter = faster rebound, for many small bumps)
petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.1 Damping (Softer Rear: very easy to drive, can be thrown into turns, more rear traction while accelerating)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Oil (corroboration: lighter oil more responsive, better for bumps, allows more chassis roll)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One piston step (one larger/extra hole) at a time; adapt oil to keep low-speed feel. Bigger holes mean less pack, so the rear soaks up sharp bumps and finds traction on rough/loose sections instead of being thrown up over them.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.40 Shock Pistons (larger holes = less damping, for small bumps)
petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.2 Shock Pistons (Bigger Holes: very good for bumpy tracks, more stable and more traction in bumpy sections)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Pistons (corroboration: more/larger holes pass oil quicker = more responsive damping; rougher track = more holes)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One piston step (one smaller/fewer hole) at a time; one hole smaller feels like ~5wt thicker oil (Cheat Sheet p.40). Fewer holes add pack so the rear locks up over harsh landings and holds the jump line; too few deflects over chop.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.40 Shock Pistons (smaller holes = more damping / more pack, improve jump lifts and landings, for smoother tracks)
petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.2 Shock Pistons (Smaller Holes: more pack, good for smooth tracks with big jumps or harsh landings)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Pistons (corroboration: fewer/smaller holes pass oil slower; smoother track = fewer holes)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate softer at a time. A softer front loads the front tyres for more mid/exit steering and bump compliance — the spring lever against 4WD push; too soft makes it hook, dive and traction-roll on bite.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.1 Springs (Softer Front: more steering, especially mid and exit of the corner)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.41 Shock Springs (softer = more traction, best for small bumps)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Springs (corroboration: softer end gains grip)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate stiffer at a time. A stiffer front cuts roll and dive and calms a darty/traction-rolling front on high bite; too stiff and the front pushes and loses low-speed steering.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.1 Springs (Stiffer Front: less front traction and steering, jumps better; on high-grip tracks stiffen the front, makes the car easier to drive and faster)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.41 Shock Springs (stiffer = less traction, lifts higher off jumps, better suspension response)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Springs (corroboration: stiffer end reduces roll, loses grip)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate softer at a time. A softer rear lets the rear squat and load the tyres for forward bite and rough-track traction; on high bite it brings on traction roll.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.1 Springs (Softer Rear: generally more rear traction, in turns as well as through bumps and while accelerating)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.41 Shock Springs (softer = more traction, great on rear for off-road)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Springs (corroboration: softer end gains grip)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate stiffer at a time. A stiffer rear cuts rear roll/traction-roll and adds mid-and-exit steering on high bite (especially in long fast corners); too stiff and rear traction drops on low grip.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.1 Springs (Stiffer Rear: more steering in the middle and exit of the turn, especially in long high-speed corners; rear traction reduced)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.41 Shock Springs (stiffer = creates less traction, better suspension response)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Springs (corroboration: stiffer end reduces roll, loses grip)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.25-0.5deg more negative at a time (typical -1 to -2deg front; bumpy tracks up to -2 to -3deg). Loads the outer front tyre through the corner for more high-speed cornering traction; past that the straight gets nervous.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.12 Camber, front (more = more high-speed traction through turns; shown on the B44.1 4WD buggy)
petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.3 Camber (on really bumpy tracks adding 2-3deg negative camber helps traction and reduces flipping)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Camber (corroboration: more front camber = more cornering traction, less stable on the straight)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.25-0.5deg more negative at a time (typical -2deg rear). More rear camber adds mid-corner rear grip when the track grips and rolls; it costs straight-line forward acceleration, so don't chase it on loose dirt.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.15 Camber, rear (more negative = more high-speed traction through corners; shown on the B44.1 4WD buggy)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Camber (corroboration: more rear camber = more cornering traction, less forward traction)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.25-0.5deg toward 0 at a time; never go positive. Standing the rear tyres up puts more flat patch down for forward bite and acceleration; too little and mid-corner rear grip drops.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.15 Camber, rear (less negative / 0deg = more straight-line acceleration)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Camber (corroboration: less rear camber = more straight-line acceleration, less cornering traction)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One caster-block step (~2-3deg) at a time. More caster aids straight-line and bump stability and adds on-power exit drive; it trades away off-power entry turn-in, so back off if the buggy already pushes into corners.
sources: Hudy Setup Tips p.18 (Caster, Effects of Caster Adjustment — more caster angle (more inclined): increases straight-line stability, decreases off-power steering at corner entry, makes the car more stable through bumpy track conditions)
petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.1 Caster (corroboration: more caster aids stability and handling in bumpy sections)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.16 Caster, front (corroboration on stability)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One caster-block step (~2-3deg) at a time. Less caster increases off-power turn-in drastically — the buggy turns tighter and faster INTO corners; it costs straight-line and bump stability, so avoid on rough tracks. The first lever against 4WD entry push on smooth tracks.
sources: Hudy Setup Tips p.18 (Caster, Effects of Caster Adjustment — less caster angle (more vertical): decreases straight-line stability, increases off-power steering at corner entry, increases suspension efficiency)
petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.1 Caster (corroboration: less caster increases steering drastically, the car turns tighter and faster)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.16 Caster, front (corroboration)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.25-0.5deg toward toe-out at a time, both sides equal; NEVER more than 2deg total front toe-out (Buggy Guide). Sharpens turn-in to fight 4WD push; too much makes the front wandery and unstable in bumps and on the straight.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.3 Toe (Front Toe-out: increases turn-in steering a lot; never use more than 2 degrees)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.49 Toe-in/toe-out, front (toe-out = quicker corner turn-in, unstable in bumps and on slippery straights)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Toe (corroboration: front toe-out = more initial turn-in)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.25-0.5deg toward toe-in at a time, both sides. Calms a nervous front and smooths exit steering and straight-line stability for an easier-to-drive car; too much dulls initial turn-in.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.3 Toe (Front Toe-in: stabilizes the car in the straights and coming out of turns, smoothes steering, very easy to drive)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.49 Toe-in/toe-out, front (0deg toe standard; toe-out is the unstable extreme, so toe-in calms it)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Toe (corroboration: front toe-in adds straight-line stability)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5deg more toe-in at a time (typical ~3deg total); rear NEVER runs toe-out. Adds rear stability and forward bite for low grip, but more toe-in makes the difference between sticking and breaking loose more abrupt (Buggy Guide) and slows rotation.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.3 Toe (Rear Toe-in: stabilizes the car greatly, makes the rear end 'stick'; more toe-in makes the difference between sticking and breaking loose bigger)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Toe (corroboration: more rear toe-in = more forward traction, less rotation; best for low traction)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5deg less toe-in at a time; never reach toe-out (Buggy Guide: rear toe-out makes the car very unstable). Frees rotation and top speed on high bite to fight 4WD push; costs rear stability, so back off on low grip.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.3 Toe (Rear Toe-in stabilizes and reduces rotation, so less toe-in frees rotation; Rear Toe-out is never used)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Toe (corroboration: less rear toe-in = more rotation and top speed, for high-traction surfaces)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1mm at a time via threaded collar/preload, keep front-rear rake intact. Lower feels more direct, corners a bit faster and is harder to flip on high bite; too low and it bottoms and skates over bumps.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.2 Ride Height (Lower: feels more direct, can corner faster, harder to flip the car over)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.29-30 Ride Height front/rear (lower = less rear-end sliding / more push; shown on B44.1 4WD buggy)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Ride Height (corroboration: lower = more responsive, worse for bumps/jumps)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1mm at a time via threaded collar/preload. Higher clears bumps and jumps better and adds acceleration in loose terrain; too high feels tippy and can flip in high-grip conditions, so don't over-raise on smooth high bite.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.2 Ride Height (Higher: better in bumps, jumps better; can feel tippy or flip in high-grip conditions)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.30 Ride Height, rear (higher = better acceleration in loose terrain, better lift off jumps)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Ride Height (corroboration: higher = better in bumps and jumps, less responsive)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5-1mm more front down-travel (or one fewer internal limiter) at a time, identical L/R, keep front and rear droop about equal on low grip. More droop gives better handling and more consistent traction on bumpy/difficult tracks and lands jumps better; it makes the car less direct.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.4 Internal Travel Limiters / Droop (Less (more droop): better handling on bumpy tracks, more consistent traction, lands better after jumps)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.42 Shock Travel Limiters (fewer limiters = for bumpy tracks)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Droop (corroboration: more droop = more weight transfer, better over bumps, less responsive)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5-1mm less front down-travel (or one more internal limiter) at a time, identical L/R. Less droop changes direction faster, corners flatter and is the most effective way to reduce traction rolls (Buggy Guide); only advisable on smooth tracks.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.4 Internal Travel Limiters / Droop (More (less droop): changes direction faster, corners flatter, more responsive; adding limiters is the most effective way of reducing traction rolls)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.42 Shock Travel Limiters (more limiters used when the car leans too much in turns)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Droop (corroboration: less droop = more responsive, less traction rolling)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5-1mm more rear down-travel (or one fewer limiter) at a time, identical L/R. More rear droop lets the rear extend to find grip over bumps for forward bite and better landings; the end with the LEAST droop feels most stable, so adding rear droop trades some stability.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.4 Internal Travel Limiters / Droop (Less limiters/more droop: more consistent traction on difficult tracks, lands better; the end with the least downtravel feels the most stable)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.42 Shock Travel Limiters (fewer limiters = for bumpy tracks)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Droop (corroboration: more rear droop = more stable over bumps)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5-1mm less rear down-travel (or one more limiter) at a time, identical L/R. Less rear droop keeps the rear flat and direct for braking stability and traction-roll resistance on high bite; it costs rear traction over rough ground.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.4 Internal Travel Limiters / Droop (More limiters/less droop: corners flatter, more responsive; the end with least downtravel feels most stable and direct; most effective way to reduce traction rolls)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.42 Shock Travel Limiters (more limiters used when car leans too much in turns)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Droop (corroboration: less rear droop = more stable under braking, less over bumps)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One shim/insert step (~1deg) at a time, both sides. More anti-squat makes the rear more throttle-sensitive for forward traction on high bite; a lot (4deg+) can make the rear break loose accelerating and lift more on jumps.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.8 Anti-squat, off-road (more anti-squat = less side traction in corners, more rear lift in jumps)
petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.2 Anti-Squat (More: rear more sensitive to throttle, more powering out of corners on high traction; 4deg+ can make the rear break loose)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Anti-Squat (corroboration: more anti-squat = more forward traction, more rear lift on jumps)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One shim/insert step (~1deg) at a time, both sides. Less anti-squat gives more side-bite and more rear traction accelerating on slippery/dusty/bumpy tracks, and makes the rear feel very stable (power-sliding easier); it trades away some straight-line forward bite on high grip.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.8 Anti-squat, off-road (less anti-squat = more side traction in corners, more rear traction for slick or bumpy surfaces)

petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.2 Anti-Squat (Less: more rear traction accelerating on slippery/dusty tracks, more side-bite, accelerates better through bumpy sections; very little makes the rear very stable)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Anti-Squat (corroboration: less anti-squat = more side traction, better on slick/bumpy)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wire size (~0.1mm) thicker at a time, ONLY if the chassis has a front bar mount (refuse otherwise and fall back to front spring). A stiffer front bar reduces front roll and 'hooking' and gives the rear more grip; it reduces low-speed steering, so avoid on loose/low-bite tracks.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.4 Anti-Roll bar (Stiffer Front: reduces low-speed steering, reduces hooking by preventing front-end roll, more rear traction in turns; bars best on smooth high-traction tracks only)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.7 Anti-roll Bars (stiffer/thicker bars for high traction tracks; front bar helps a car that is oversteering)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Anti-Roll Bar (corroboration: thicker front bar = less roll, more rear grip, for high-traction tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wire size (~0.1mm) thinner at a time (or remove the bar; on a bumpy track use a very thin one). A softer/removed front bar adds front roll and low-speed steering to fight push on low-grip/rough tracks; on high bite it can bring on front traction roll.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.4 Anti-Roll bar (stiffer front reduces low-speed steering, so softer/removed front adds it; bars reduce traction at that end; if you must use one on a bumpy track use a very thin one)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.7 Anti-roll Bars (softer/thinner bars for low and medium bite tracks)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Anti-Roll Bar (corroboration: thinner front bar = more roll, for low-medium traction)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wire size (~0.1mm) thicker at a time, ONLY if a rear bar mount exists (refuse otherwise, fall back to rear spring/shock position). A stiffer rear bar gives more steering (the car steers tighter, even at low speed) and resists traction roll; it costs rear side traction, so avoid on loose dirt.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.4 Anti-Roll bar (Stiffer Rear: more steering, steers tighter also at low speed; bars best on smooth high-traction tracks only and reduce traction at that end)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.7 Anti-roll Bars (stiffer/thicker bars for high traction tracks)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Anti-Roll Bar (corroboration: thicker rear bar = more on-power steering, less roll, for high-traction tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wire size (~0.1mm) thinner at a time (or remove). A softer/removed rear bar adds rear roll and side traction for low-grip/rough tracks; on high bite it can bring on traction roll.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.4 Anti-Roll bar (stiffer rear adds steering and reduces traction at the rear, so softer/removed adds rear traction; on bumpy tracks use a very thin bar or none)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.7 Anti-roll Bars (softer/thinner bars for low and medium bite tracks)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Anti-Roll Bar (corroboration: thinner rear bar = more roll and rear grip, for low-medium traction)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One washer / one link step at a time; re-check front camber after. A lower front roll centre (or longer link) lets the front roll and dive more for more mid-corner steering and peak grip on smooth high-traction surfaces; it is less reactive. Watch the front/rear balance.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.31/34 Roll Centre (lower roll centre = leans more cornering, less responsive/more forgiving, for high-traction tracks)
petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.3 Roll Center / Camber links (Longer Front: front rolls and dives more, lots of mid-corner steering)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Roll Center (corroboration: lower roll centre = more roll, more grip, less responsive)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One washer / one link step at a time; re-check front camber. A higher front roll centre (or shorter link) makes the front more reactive with more turn-in and stabilizes it in bumps; used when traction is low. It costs mid-corner steering.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.31/34 Roll Centre (higher roll centre = more responsive, for low-traction tracks)
petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.3 Roll Center / Camber links (Shorter Front: front feels stable, a little more turn-in, less mid-corner steering)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Roll Center (corroboration: higher roll centre = more responsive, less roll)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One washer / one link step at a time; keep enough rear camber or you lose rear traction (Buggy Guide), and re-check rear camber after. A lower rear roll centre (longer link) gives more rear traction in and out of turns with very progressive, predictable slide on high bite; less reactive.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.3 Roll Center / Camber links (Longer Rear: more rear traction in turns and coming out of them, rear slide very progressive; make sure there's enough rear camber)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.31/34 Roll Centre (lower roll centre = more grip / leans more, for high-traction tracks)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Roll Center (corroboration: lower rear roll centre = more rear grip and roll)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One washer / one link step at a time; re-check rear camber. A higher rear roll centre (shorter link) makes the rear feel very stable and adds turn-in/steering and stabilizes it in bumps for low-traction tracks; the rear breaks later but more suddenly, and it costs some rear cornering traction.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.3 Roll Center / Camber links (Shorter Rear: rear feels very stable, breaks out later and more suddenly, makes the front dive a little more = more steering)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.31/34 Roll Centre (higher roll centre = more responsive, for low-traction tracks)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Roll Center (corroboration: higher rear roll centre = more responsive, less rear roll)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Move one shim, both sides. A shorter wheelbase makes the car nimble and quicker in tight turns and shifts weight back for more rear traction; it costs high-speed stability, so avoid it on wide/jumpy tracks.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.2 Wheelbase (Shorter: very nimble, good in tight turns, for small tight tracks without big jumps or bumps)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.51 Wheelbase (shorter = more rear traction, weight shifted to back)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Wheelbase (corroboration: shorter = more agility and rotation)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Move one shim, both sides. A longer wheelbase is a lot more stable and better in wide high-speed turns and over bumps/jumps; it makes turn-in slower, so avoid on tight tracks.
sources: petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.2 Wheelbase (Longer: a lot more stable, better in wide high-speed turns, good on wide-open tracks)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.51 Wheelbase (longer = better stability, slightly more steering)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Wheelbase (corroboration: longer = more high-speed and jump stability)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Move the pack/weight one position rearward (or add a rear ballast weight) and re-check ride height after. Rearward bias adds rear traction and stability under acceleration and braking for low grip; it reduces steering and changes direction slower, so don't over-do it if the car already pushes.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.50 Weight Distribution (rear weight = less steering, more rear traction, more stable under acceleration and braking; B44.1 4WD buggy example)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.58 Battery Placement (battery is a large mass used to tune front/rear balance)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Weight (corroboration: rearward bias adds forward bite, reduces steering)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Move the pack/weight one position forward and re-check ride height after. Forward bias adds steering while accelerating to fight 4WD push; it makes the car change direction slower in transitions, jump more nose-down, and reduces rear traction — so back off on loose/low-grip tracks.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.50 Weight Distribution (front weight = more steering while accelerating, changes direction slower, more nose-down jumping)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.58 Battery Placement (battery mass tunes front/rear balance)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Weight (corroboration: forward bias adds steering, reduces rear traction)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1/8 turn looser at a time, ONLY if the car has a slipper (many 1/10 4WD use a centre diff instead — refuse and tune the centre diff there). A looser slipper cushions the power hit so the tyres hook up instead of spinning on low traction; too loose wastes acceleration and overheats.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.43 Slipper Clutch (looser = for tracks with low traction, more traction exiting corner)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Slipper (corroboration: looser slipper for low traction, cushions power)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1/8 turn tighter at a time, only if a slipper is fitted. A tighter slipper gives more instant acceleration and smoother corner entry on high bite; on low grip it lets the tyres spin, so loosen rather than tighten on loose/slick tracks.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.43 Slipper Clutch (tighter = for high-bite tracks, more instant acceleration, smoother corner entry)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Slipper (corroboration: tighter slipper = more direct drive on high bite)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Step one compound softer (or change tread to match the surface — tyres are the first thing to get right). Softer rears add forward bite on low-bite/cold surfaces but overheat on high bite/hot — match compound to surface and temperature first.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.45 Tyre Compound (softer compound for smoother surfaces and higher temperatures)
petitrc Buggy Setup Guide (BuggySetupGuide.pdf) p.1 Tires (tyres are always the first element in setting up a car; if you've got the right tyres you're 90% there)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Tyres (corroboration: softer compound adds grip on low bite, wears and heats faster)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Step one compound harder. On high-bite/hot/abrasive surfaces a harder rear stays cooler and keeps consistent grip where a soft tyre would grease over; useless on cold/loose tracks. Bumpier and wet/grass surfaces also favour a harder compound (Cheat Sheet p.45).
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.45 Tyre Compound (harder compound for bumpier surfaces, for grass, for wet conditions)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Tyres (corroboration: harder compound for high-bite/abrasive/hot, lasts longer)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Step one insert firmer. A firmer insert holds the carcass up under load for less rolling resistance and better cornering support to resist traction roll on high bite; too firm causes the car to bounce and lose traction (Cheat Sheet p.46), and on rough/loose ground it stops the tyre conforming.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.46 Tyre Inserts (harder = less rolling resistance, better cornering; too firm an insert causes the car to bounce and lose traction)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Inserts (corroboration: firmer insert adds support and steering on high bite)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Step one insert softer. A softer insert gives more traction and lets the tyre wrap rough/loose ground for mechanical grip; too light a foam makes the car wander and become unstable (Cheat Sheet p.46), and on high bite it folds and traction-rolls.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.46 Tyre Inserts (softer = more traction, more drag; too light a foam makes the car wander and be very unstable)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Inserts (corroboration: softer insert conforms on rough/low-bite tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One pinion tooth at a time, then check motor temp after a run (keep well under the motor's limit). Taller gearing (more pinion teeth) adds top speed for long straights but pulls harder on the motor and runs hotter and uses more battery — back off if it runs hot.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.28 Pinion Gear (more teeth = more top speed, less run time, gear ratio goes up)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Gearing (corroboration: more pinion = more top speed, less acceleration, more heat)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One pinion tooth at a time. Shorter gearing (fewer pinion teeth) adds punch off slow corners on tight tracks, runs cooler and gives more run time; it tops out earlier, so don't over-gear-down for long straights.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.28 Pinion Gear (fewer teeth = more acceleration, more run time, gear ratio goes down)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Gearing (corroboration: fewer pinion teeth = more acceleration, less top speed, cooler)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~2.5wt / ~50-100 cSt) thicker at a time. The Slash ships 30wt; the spec guide runs 60wt rear for ample pack on jump landings and to keep the tall body's chassis roll to a minimum. Too thick kills forward bite over bumps.
sources: Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Shock oil (rears filled with 60wt: ample 'pack' for jump landings, keeps chassis roll to a minimum)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.39 Shock Fluid (higher viscosity / thicker = less bottoming out)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~2.5wt) thinner at a time. Frees the rear to follow rough ground for forward bite and faster rebound over small bumps; too thin lets the heavy body roll and wallow.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.39 Shock Fluid (lower viscosity / thinner = faster rebound for many small bumps)
Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Shock oil (stock 30wt lets the suspension absorb bumps easily at slower speeds)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~2.5wt) thicker at a time. The spec Slash runs 50wt front — lighter than the 60wt rear because the SC front end is much lighter — to balance the chassis and keep it from bottoming harshly. Too thick makes the front skate over bumps and steering go lazy.
sources: Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Shock oil (front filled with 50wt, lighter than rear because the front end is much lighter, to balance feel and set the chassis up in the corners)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.39 Shock Fluid (thicker / heavier = less bottoming out)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~2.5wt) thinner at a time. Frees the front to react quicker on turn-in and follow rough ground; too thin lets the front dive on braking and off jumps.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.39 Shock Fluid (lower viscosity / thinner = faster rebound for many small bumps)
Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Shock oil (lighter damping up front balances the lighter front end)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One piston step (one smaller hole) at a time; the Cheat Sheets note one smaller hole feels like ~+5wt thicker oil. Fewer/smaller holes add pack so the SC body holds up on big landings; too few and it deflects over chop.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.40 Shock Pistons (smaller holes = more damping / more 'pack', improve jump lifts and landings, for smoother tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One piston step (one larger hole) at a time. Larger holes free the rear over small bumps for compliance and forward bite; pair with oil — pistons set the high/low-speed split, oil sets overall rate. Too free loses landing pack.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.40 Shock Pistons (larger holes = less damping, for small bumps)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Move the lower shock mount out one hole on the arm (the Slash has 5 rear positions; base is 2nd from inside). Outer reduces body roll and sharpens agility on smooth tracks with small jumps; on a bumpy track the lost down-travel makes the chassis bounce.
sources: Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Shock Position (moving shocks outward decreases the arm's leverage, making the suspension stiffer; smooth tracks with small jumps benefit from moving out one hole to reduce body roll and enhance agility; a bumpy track lacks down-travel and bounces)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.37 Shock Mounting, rear suspension arm (outer hole stiffer, less responsive, more locked in)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Move the lower shock mount in one hole on the arm. Inner adds down-travel and softness to soak up bumps and jumps; too far in adds body roll on a tall SC truck and can bring on traction roll on bite.
sources: Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Shock Position (moving shocks inward softens the suspension; the base inner/2nd-hole setup offers ample down-travel to soak up bumps and jumps)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.37 Shock Mounting, rear suspension arm (inner hole softer, good for bumps and jumps)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Move the front lower mount out one hole (the Slash front has 2 positions; base is the inner hole). Outer stiffens the front and cuts roll for smooth high-bite tracks; on bumps the lost travel makes the front skip.
sources: Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Shock Position (two front positions; base inner hole; moving outward stiffens the suspension)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.35 Shock Mounting, front suspension arm (outer hole stiffer, more stable)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Add one internal limiter (~1mm) at a time, both rear shocks equal. On a tall, roll-prone SC truck a rear limiter curbs squat and lean so the body stops flopping into traction roll; too much and it deflects over rough ground.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.42 Shock Travel Limiters (more limiters used in side shocks when the car leans too much in turns; in rear shocks they add traction when the front rises on acceleration; fewer for bumpy tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Remove one internal limiter (~1mm) at a time, both rear shocks equal. Fewer limiters free up travel so the truck soaks up a bumpy track; too few and the heavy body leans into traction roll on bite.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.42 Shock Travel Limiters (fewer limiters for bumpy tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate softer at a time. A softer rear loads the tyres for forward bite on low grip and small bumps; on high-bite surfaces a tall SC truck will roll over, so don't soften on astroturf/carpet.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.41 Shock Springs (softer / lighter tension great on rear for off-road, gives more traction, best for small bumps)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate stiffer at a time. A stiffer rear cuts the tall body's roll and traction-roll on high bite and lifts cleaner off jumps; too stiff and it loses rear traction on low grip.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.41 Shock Springs (stiffer / heavier tension creates less traction, lifts higher off jumps, better suspension response)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate softer at a time. A softer front loads the front tyres for steering and bump compliance; on very high bite a tall SC front dives and traction-rolls, so don't soften on astroturf/carpet.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.41 Shock Springs (softer / lighter tension gives more traction, best for small bumps)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate stiffer at a time. A stiffer front cuts front roll and dive and calms a darty SC front on high bite; too stiff and the front pushes.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.41 Shock Springs (stiffer / heavier tension creates less traction, better suspension response)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.25-0.5deg more negative at a time. The spec Slash bases -2.0deg front for a good contact patch through the corner, and dials in more on heavily rutted tracks. Loads the outer front tyre when the body leans; too much costs straight-line patch.
sources: Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Camber Front (base -2.0deg gives a good contact patch through the corner; more on heavily rutted tracks)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.12 Camber, front (more / 2deg = more high-speed traction through turns; less / 0deg = more straight-line acceleration)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.25-0.5deg more negative at a time. The spec Slash bases -2.5deg rear and tunes it by how much rear traction the track needs. More rear camber adds mid-corner grip when the body leans; it costs straight-line forward traction.
sources: Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Camber Rear (base -2.5deg; changed based on how much rear traction the track needs)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.15 Camber, rear (less / -2deg = more high-speed traction through corners; more / 2+deg removes straight-line acceleration)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.25-0.5deg toward 0 at a time; never go positive. Standing the rear tyres up puts a flatter patch down for forward bite and acceleration; too little and mid-corner rear grip drops.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.15 Camber, rear (less negative / toward 0 = more straight-line acceleration)
Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Camber Rear (rear camber set by how much rear traction is needed)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One caster step at a time. More caster steadies the heavy SC body on the straight and adds on-power exit drive and bump stability; it trades away off-power entry turn-in. (SC10/Slash kingpin caster is set by the caster blocks.)
sources: Hudy Setup Tips p.18 (Caster, Effects of Caster Adjustment — more caster angle (more inclined): increases straight-line stability, decreases off-power steering at corner entry, makes the car more stable through bumpy track conditions)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.16 Caster, front (corroboration: SC10 short-course truck pictured)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One caster step at a time. Less caster sharpens off-power turn-in ENTERING corners; it costs straight-line and bump stability — avoid on rough/loose tracks where the tall SC body needs the stability.
sources: Hudy Setup Tips p.18 (Caster, Effects of Caster Adjustment — less caster angle (more vertical): decreases straight-line stability, increases off-power steering at corner entry, increases suspension efficiency)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.16 Caster, front (corroboration: SC10 short-course truck pictured)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5deg toward toe-out at a time, both steering links equal. The spec Slash bases 1.0deg toe-out per side; toe-out increases 'instant' steering response. Too much makes the front nervous and unstable in bumps. Rear toe on a Slash is fixed by the suspension design — front only.
sources: Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Toe front only (toe-out increases 'instant' steering response; base 1.0deg toe-out per side; rear toe is preset/not adjustable on the Slash)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.49 Toe-in/toe-out front (toe-out = quicker corner turn-in, unstable in bumps and slippery)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5deg toward toe-in at a time, both links equal. Per the Slash guide, front toe-IN gives better straight-line stability and more steering through and out of a corner; too much dulls initial turn-in. Zero toe is a safe SC baseline.
sources: Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Toe front only (toe-in provides better straight-line stability and more steering through and out of a corner)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.49 Toe-in/toe-out front (0deg toe standard for all conditions)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Lower 1mm at a time via preload clips/collar, keep the bones-level rake intact. A lower stance on a tall SC truck cuts roll and the chance of flipping in corners on smooth high bite; too low and it bottoms and skates on bumps.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.29 Ride Height, front (lower = less chance of flipping in corners; higher = more chassis roll, better traction on bumpy tracks)
Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Shock Preload and Ride Height (set via preload clips/collar; base bones-level, rear a little below level)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Raise 1mm at a time via preload. Raises clearance for rough/rutted tracks and better lift off jumps; too high adds roll on a tall SC body and dulls response — don't over-raise on smooth high bite.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.30 Ride Height, rear (higher = better acceleration in loose terrain, better lift off jumps; lower = less rear-end sliding in corners)
Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Shock Preload and Ride Height (raising the rear gives more aggressive turn-in and more on-power grip)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5-1mm more front down-travel at a time (set by shock position / limiter), identical L/R. More front droop lets the front extend and shift weight rearward on power for on-power steering and bump grip; it softens high-speed stability.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.23 Droop (more droop / more shock travel for rougher, lower-traction tracks; less for smooth high-traction tracks)
Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Shock Position (down travel is reduced by moving the lower shock mount further out; ample down travel soaks up bumps)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5-1mm less front down-travel at a time, identical L/R. Less front droop keeps the front flatter to reduce roll and steady the truck on smooth high bite; it costs on-power steering and bump compliance.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.23 Droop (less droop / less shock travel for smooth, high-traction tracks; reduces chassis roll)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5-1mm more rear down-travel at a time, identical L/R. More rear droop lets the rear extend to find grip over bumps for forward bite; it reduces braking stability.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.23 Droop (more droop / more shock travel for rougher, lower-traction tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5-1mm less rear down-travel at a time, identical L/R. Less rear droop keeps the rear flat for braking stability and flatter jumping; it costs rear traction over rough ground.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.23 Droop (less droop / less shock travel for smooth, high-traction tracks; reduces chassis roll)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One shim/insert step (~1deg, shims under the front of the rear arm mounts) at a time, both sides. More anti-squat plants the rear for forward bite on smooth grip; it cuts side traction and lifts the rear more in jumps and unsettles bumpy on-power sections.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.8 Anti-squat, off-road (more anti-squat = less side traction in corners, more rear lift in jumps; change by shimming the rear arm mounts higher)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One shim/insert step (~1deg) flatter at a time, both sides. Less anti-squat adds side bite and rear traction for slick or bumpy surfaces and frees on-power steering; it trades away some straight-line forward bite.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.8 Anti-squat, off-road (less anti-squat = more side traction in corners, more rear traction for slick or bumpy surfaces)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Move the rear upper camber link to the UPPER tower position (Slash has upper/lower). It decreases the contact patch slightly as the body leans, freeing the rear to rotate for more turn-in on tight tracks; it slightly reduces overall rear grip. (Slash: trim a little tower material for full up-travel.)
sources: Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Roll Center rear only (upper position frees the rear to rotate for more steering/turn-in; lower/stock gives the most rear stability)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.31 Roll Centre (raising roll centre for low-traction tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Move the rear upper camber link to the LOWER (stock) tower position. It loads the rear contact patch progressively as the body leans, giving the most rear stability and grip through the corner; it costs aggressive turn-in. This is the Slash base setup.
sources: Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Roll Center rear only (lower/stock location provides the most stability for the rear end, maintains traction as the chassis leans)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.31 Roll Centre (lowering roll centre for high-traction tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wire size (~0.1mm) thicker at a time, ONLY if the SC truck has a rear bar mount (many SC trucks ship without one — refuse and fall back to rear spring / shock position otherwise). A stiffer rear bar cuts the tall body's roll and traction-roll on high bite; it costs rear side traction on low grip.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.7 Anti-roll Bars, Sway Bars (stiffer/thicker bars for high traction tracks; thicker minimizes chassis roll, more responsive)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wire size (~0.1mm) thinner at a time (or remove the bar). Adds rear roll and side traction for low-grip/rough tracks; on high bite a tall SC body can traction-roll, so don't over-soften there.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.7 Anti-roll Bars, Sway Bars (softer/thinner bars for low and med bite tracks; more chassis roll)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wire size (~0.1mm) thicker at a time, ONLY if a front bar mount exists (refuse and fall back to front spring otherwise). A thicker front bar cuts front roll and traction-roll on high bite; on low grip it pushes. Cheat Sheets: a thicker FRONT bar than rear helps an oversteering car.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.7 Anti-roll Bars (if oversteering, add a front anti-roll bar / make the front bar thicker than the rear; thicker bars for high-traction tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wire size (~0.1mm) thinner at a time (or remove). Adds front roll and front grip for low-grip/rough tracks; on high bite a tall SC front can traction-roll, so don't over-soften.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.7 Anti-roll Bars (if understeering, add a rear bar / make the rear thicker than front; thinner/softer bars for low-med bite tracks, more chassis roll)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Step up one fluid weight at a time. On a 2WD Slash the planetary diff is tuned with a SMALL amount of very thick (~300K) lube; on a 4WD SC the rear gear diff takes a thicker oil. Thicker tightens the diff for on-power stability and forward bite on high grip; it costs corner-entry steering. For loose tracks use thinner/looser.
sources: Traxxas Slash Spec Racing Setup Guide — Differential (use a very thick ~300Kwt diff fluid, a small amount, for consistent diff action that holds up for weeks)
AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.21 Diff Fluid, Rear Diff off-road (thicker/heavier = less grip but more stability on power, for high-traction conditions)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Step down one fluid weight at a time. A thinner/looser rear diff lets the inside rear differentiate for smoother power-down and more rotation/grip on slick or bumpy tracks; it costs on-power stability on high bite.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.21 Diff Fluid, Rear Diff off-road (thinner/lighter = more grip but less stability on power, for low-traction conditions)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 4WD SC ONLY (refuse on a 2WD truck with no front diff). Step up one fluid weight. A thicker front gear diff calms entry steering and adds mid-corner front traction and on-power stability for high bite; it pushes on low grip.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.19 Diff Fluid, Front Diff off-road (thicker/heavier = less steering but more stability on power, for high-traction conditions)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 4WD SC ONLY (refuse on a 2WD truck). Step down one fluid weight. A thinner front gear diff frees corner-entry and mid-corner steering for low grip; too thin makes the car inconsistent through the corner.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.19 Diff Fluid, Front Diff off-road (thinner/lighter = more steering but less stability, for low-traction conditions)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1/8 turn looser at a time. A looser slipper cushions the power hit so the rears hook up instead of spinning on low grip, and protects the drivetrain on jump landings; too loose wastes acceleration and overheats.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.43 Slipper Clutch (looser for tracks with low traction, more traction exiting corner)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1/8 turn tighter at a time. A tighter slipper delivers more instant acceleration and smoother corner entry on high bite; on low grip it lets the rears spin up, so loosen rather than tighten on loose/slick tracks.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.43 Slipper Clutch (tighter for high bite tracks, more instant acceleration, smoother corner entry)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Shift the pack rearward one step (the SC10 uses a cuttable foam spacer to move the battery). Rearward weight adds rear traction and stability under power/braking; it costs steering. On extreme high/low traction tracks moving the battery can rebalance the truck for better rear grip.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.58 Battery Placement (rearward = less steering, more rear traction; SC10 short-course truck pictured; on extreme-traction tracks moving the battery rebalances the car for better rear traction)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Shift the pack forward one step. Forward weight adds steering (changes direction slower but bites more) and more nose-down jumping; it costs rear traction. Don't chase it on low grip where the rear needs the weight.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.58 Battery Placement (forward = more steering, less rear traction); p.50 Weight Distribution (front weight = more steering while accelerating, more nose-down jumping)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Move one wheelbase shim per side. A longer wheelbase adds high-speed-corner and rough-track stability and better jumping on a tall SC truck; it slows turn-in, so shorten for tight technical tracks.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.51 Wheelbase (longer = slightly more steering [bias forward], better stability; SC) plus p.17 Chassis Length (longer = more stability in high-speed corners, better on rough tracks, better jumping, slower turn-in)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Move one wheelbase shim per side. A shorter wheelbase shifts weight back for more rear traction and quicker left-right turning on tight tracks; it costs high-speed and jumping stability.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.51 Wheelbase (shorter = wheels closer, more rear traction, weight shifted back; quicker left-right turning per p.17 Chassis Length)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Step one compound softer (and match tread to the surface first). Softer rears add forward bite on low-bite/cold/smoother surfaces; on bumpy/abrasive/hot tracks they overheat and wear fast — match compound to surface and temperature.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.45 Tyre Compound (softer compound for smoother surfaces and higher temperatures)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Step one compound harder. On bumpy/abrasive/hot (or wet/grass) surfaces a harder rear stays consistent where a soft tyre greases over; useless on cold/smooth low-bite tracks.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.45 Tyre Compound (harder compound for bumpier surfaces, for grass, for wet conditions)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Step one insert firmer. A firmer rear insert holds the carcass up under the heavy SC body to resist traction roll and fold on high bite; too firm makes the truck bounce and lose grip on rough ground.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.46 Tyre Inserts, foam (harder = less rolling resistance, better cornering; too firm causes the car to bounce and lose traction)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Step one insert softer. A softer rear insert lets the tyre wrap rough/loose ground for mechanical grip; under a heavy SC body on high bite it folds and traction-rolls, so don't soften on astroturf/carpet.
sources: AE RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.46 Tyre Inserts, foam (softer = more traction, more drag; too light a foam makes the car wander and be unstable)
