rules.magnitude_guidance: Shim the front of the rear arm mounts up ~1 deg at a time (AE p.8: shims under the front of the rear arm mounts). More anti-squat plants the rear for drive off the corner; on a tall stadium truck too much costs side bite and can trip a traction-roll on a high-grip corner.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.8 'Anti-squat, off-road' — more anti-squat: less side traction in corners, more rear lift in jumps
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Anti-Squat (corroboration: more anti-squat adds forward traction on acceleration, reduces it off-power)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Remove a shim from the front of the rear arm mounts, ~1 deg flatter at a time (AE p.8). Flatter arms give more side traction and smoother drive over slick/bumpy ground — the safer direction on a high-CG truck that wants to roll; too flat loses forward bite on smooth high-grip.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.8 'Anti-squat, off-road' — less anti-squat: more side traction in corners, more rear traction for slick or bumpy surfaces
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Anti-Squat (corroboration: less anti-squat frees off-power rear traction and smooths bumpy acceleration)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One caster-block step at a time (~2 deg). More caster steadies a twitchy truck on the straight, adds on-power exit drive and bump stability; it trades away off-power turn-in, so back off if the truck already pushes on entry.
sources: Hudy Setup Tips p.18 (Caster, Effects of Caster Adjustment — more caster angle (more inclined): increases straight-line stability, decreases off-power steering at corner entry, makes the car more stable through bumpy track conditions)
Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.16 'Caster, front' (corroboration: more caster adds straight-line stability and on-power/exit drive steering)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One caster-block step at a time (~2 deg). Less caster sharpens off-power turn-in for tight smooth tracks; it costs straight-line and bump stability — risky on a tall truck on a fast/rough track.
sources: Hudy Setup Tips p.18 (Caster, Effects of Caster Adjustment — less caster angle (more vertical): decreases straight-line stability, increases off-power steering at corner entry, increases suspension efficiency)
Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.16 'Caster, front' (corroboration: less caster adds off-power/initial turn-in, reduces straight-line stability)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5 deg at a time, both steering rods equally (AE p.49 calls 1 deg toe-out a typical setting). Adds quicker turn-in; AE warns it is unstable in bumps and slippery — back off on a rough/low-grip stadium track.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.49 'Toe-in, toe-out, front' — toe-out: quicker corner turn-in, unstable in bumps and slippery
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Toe (corroboration: front toe-out sharpens corner entry / turn-in)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5 deg at a time toward 0 deg toe (AE p.49: 0 deg is the standard, stable-in-all-conditions setting). Calms a darty front and steadies the truck over bumps and on slippery ground at the cost of some turn-in bite.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.49 'Toe-in, toe-out, front' — 0 deg toe standard for all conditions; toe-out unstable in bumps and slippery
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Toe (corroboration: reducing toe-out toward zero calms steering and adds entry stability)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5 deg more negative at a time (AE p.12 cites ~2 deg as the high-traction-through-turns setting). Re-check front toe after — they interact. Loads the outer front tyre for more grip through fast corners.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.12 'Camber, front' — more (2 deg) camber: more high-speed traction through turns
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Camber (corroboration: more negative front camber raises peak cornering grip, costs straight-line patch)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5 deg more negative at a time (AE p.15: more negative rear camber → more high-speed traction through corners). Helps a tall truck hold the rear through a high-grip corner; too much costs forward bite off the corner.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.15 'Camber, rear' — less (-2 deg): more high-speed traction through corners
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Camber (corroboration: more negative rear camber adds cornering grip, costs straight-line/forward drive)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1mm at a time via the threaded shock collar (AE p.29). Lower front drops CG for a steadier, less roll-prone truck on smooth high grip; AE notes lower front 'creates more push', so expect a touch less steering and watch for bottoming.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.29 'Ride Height, front' — lower creates more push; higher creates more steering / better traction on bumpy tracks
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Ride Height (corroboration: lower ride height lowers CG for more stability, less bump clearance)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1mm at a time via the threaded shock collar (AE p.29). Higher front adds steering and clears bumps; on a tall truck it raises CG and can promote traction-roll on high grip — go back down when the track hooks up.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.29 'Ride Height, front' — higher creates more steering, more chassis roll and better traction on bumpy tracks
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Ride Height (corroboration: raising ride height clears rough ground at the cost of stability)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1mm at a time via the threaded shock collar (AE p.30: lower rear → less rear-end sliding in corners). Lowers rear CG to settle a loose/rolling truck on high grip; too low costs forward bite in loose terrain and lift off jumps.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.30 'Ride Height, rear' — lower: less rear-end sliding in corners
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Ride Height (corroboration: lower rear ride height adds rear stability and lowers CG)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1mm at a time via the threaded shock collar (AE p.30: higher rear → better acceleration in loose terrain, better lift off jumps). Helps forward bite on loose ground and squares up jumps; raises rear CG, so back off if the truck starts to roll.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.30 'Ride Height, rear' — higher: better acceleration in loose terrain, better lift off jumps
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Ride Height (corroboration: higher rear adds rear weight transfer and forward bite, clears rough sections)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~50-100 cSt / ~2.5wt) at a time (AE p.39: thicker = less bottoming out). Holds a tall truck flatter on power and on big landings; too thick kills forward bite over chop.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.39 'Shock Fluid' — thicker/heavier (higher viscosity): less bottoming out
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Oil (corroboration: heavier oil better for smooth tracks, reduces bottoming, less responsive)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~50-100 cSt) thinner at a time (AE p.39: thinner = faster rebound for many small bumps). Frees the rear to recover over washboard for forward bite; too thin lets the rear wallow and bottom.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.39 'Shock Fluid' — thinner/lighter (lower viscosity): faster rebound for many small bumps
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Oil (corroboration: lighter oil more responsive, better for bumpy conditions)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~50-100 cSt) at a time (AE p.39: thicker = less bottoming). Slows the front to calm dive into jumps and braking twitch; too thick makes the front skate over bumps and steering go lazy.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.39 'Shock Fluid' — thicker/heavier: less bottoming out
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Oil (corroboration: heavier front oil slows dive and steering, better on smooth tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~50-100 cSt) thinner at a time (AE p.39: thinner = faster rebound over small bumps). Frees the front to follow rough ground and react quicker on turn-in; too thin lets the front dive on braking and off jumps.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.39 'Shock Fluid' — thinner/lighter: faster rebound for many small bumps
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Oil (corroboration: lighter front oil more responsive, better over bumps)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One piston step (smaller/fewer holes) at a time (AE p.40: smaller holes = more damping/pack, better jump lifts & landings, for smoother tracks). Adds pack so the rear holds up on landings; too tight and it deflects over chop. AE p.40: one hole smaller ~= +5wt oil.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.40 'Shock Pistons' — smaller holes: more damping/pack, improve jump lifts and landings, for smoother tracks
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Pistons (corroboration: fewer/smaller holes add pack/high-speed damping for jumps and smooth tracks)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One piston step (larger/more holes) at a time (AE p.40: larger holes = less damping, for small bumps). Frees the rear over bumps for forward bite; pair with the right oil — pistons set the high/low-speed split, oil sets overall rate.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.40 'Shock Pistons' — larger holes: less damping, for small bumps
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Shock Pistons (corroboration: more/larger holes free damping for bumps and low-speed compliance)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate softer at a time (AE p.41: softer is great on the rear off-road, gives more traction, best for small bumps). Adds forward bite and bump grip; on a high-CG truck too soft lets the rear roll over on grip.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.41 'Shock Springs' — softer/lighter tension: great on rear for off-road, gives more traction, best for small bumps
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Springs (corroboration: softer rear springs add forward bite and rough-track traction)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate stiffer at a time (AE p.41: stiffer creates less traction, lifts higher off jumps, better suspension response). Stiffens a rolling truck and stops squat/bottoming on high grip; AE says it costs traction, so don't stiffen on loose dirt where you need every bit of bite.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.41 'Shock Springs' — stiffer/heavier tension: creates less traction, lifts higher off jumps, better suspension response
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Springs (corroboration: stiffer rear springs reduce squat and roll, cost mechanical traction)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Add washers under the rear inner ballstud, one at a time (AE p.31/p.34). A lower rear roll centre lets the rear lean and load the tyre on high grip for drive and a more forgiving feel; re-check rear camber after.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.31 & p.34 'Roll Centre' — lower roll centre (more washers under ballstud): leans more when cornering, for high-traction tracks; lower = more forgiving, less reactive
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Roll Center (corroboration: lower rear roll centre adds roll for smoother, higher-peak rear grip)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Remove a washer from under the rear inner ballstud, one at a time (AE p.31/p.34: higher roll centre for low-traction tracks, more reactive). Cuts rear roll for quicker response and reins in roll-over on low grip; on high grip it can make the rear feel abrupt.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.31 & p.34 'Roll Centre' — raising roll centre (fewer washers under ballstud): for low-traction tracks; higher = more reactive
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Roll Center (corroboration: higher rear roll centre reduces roll for sharper, less progressive rear grip)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Move one rear-hub shim at a time, both sides (AE p.17). Longer wheelbase steadies a tall truck at speed, smooths the rough and squares up jumps at the cost of turn-in snap — the go-to for a fast bumpy stadium layout.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.17 'Chassis Length' — longer: more stability in high-speed corners, more rear traction, better on rough tracks, better jumping
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Wheelbase (corroboration: longer wheelbase adds high-speed and jumping stability, smooths the car)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Move one rear-hub shim at a time, both sides (AE p.51: shorter shifts weight back for more rear traction; p.17: more steering, quicker left-right). Wakes up a lazy truck on a tight track; gives up high-speed stability.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.17 'Chassis Length' (shorter: more steering, quicker response) & p.51 'Wheelbase' (shorter: more rear traction, weight shifted back)
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Wheelbase (corroboration: shorter wheelbase increases agility and rotation)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Loosen the slipper nut a small fraction of a turn at a time (AE p.43: looser for low-traction tracks, more traction exiting the corner). Slipping the spur cushions the power hit so a tall rear-drive truck hooks up instead of spinning; too loose and it feels soft and slow.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.43 'Slipper Clutch' — looser: for tracks with low traction, more traction exiting corner
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Slipper (corroboration: looser slipper cushions power for traction on low grip and protects the drivetrain)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Tighten the slipper nut a small fraction of a turn at a time (AE p.43: tighter for high-bite tracks, more instant acceleration, smoother corner entry). Direct drive helps on grip; on loose dirt a tight slipper just spins the rears, so don't tighten there.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.43 'Slipper Clutch' — tighter: for high bite tracks, more instant acceleration, smoother corner entry
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Slipper (corroboration: tighter slipper gives more direct drive and acceleration on high bite)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Steepen the wing one shim/step at a time (AE p.52: steeper angle = more rear traction). Adds rear downforce to steady a loose/twitchy truck down a fast straight; on a tight track it just adds drag.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.52 'Wing' — steeper angle: more rear traction
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Wing (corroboration: more wing angle adds rear downforce and high-speed stability, adds drag)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Step one compound softer (AE p.45: softer for smoother surfaces and higher track temperatures). Softer rears claw back forward bite on a low-grip/smooth surface; on a hooked-up high-CG truck more grip can promote traction-roll, and AE calls for harder rubber in the wet.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.45 'Tyre Compound' — softer compound for smoother surfaces, for higher temperatures
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Tires (corroboration: softer compound adds grip on low-bite/cold surfaces, wears and heats faster)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Step one compound harder (AE p.45: harder for bumpier surfaces, grass and wet conditions). A harder rear keeps a tall truck from over-gripping into a traction-roll and survives heat/abrasion; too hard on loose dirt loses drive entirely.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.45 'Tyre Compound' — harder compound for bumpier surfaces, for grass, for wet conditions
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Tires (corroboration: harder compound suits high-bite/abrasive/hot tracks and lasts longer)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Move the battery one mounting step rearward (AE p.58: rearward = more rear traction, less steering; p.50 mirrors for added weight). Plants a loose/wheel-spinning rear and steadies braking; costs front steering — re-check ride height after, per AE p.29/p.30.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.58 'Battery Placement' — rearward: less steering, more rear traction; p.50 'Weight Distribution': rear weight = more rear traction, more stable under acceleration and braking
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Weight/Battery Position (corroboration: rearward bias adds forward bite and reduces steering)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Move the battery one mounting step forward (AE p.58: forward = more steering, less rear traction; p.50: front weight = more steering while accelerating). Cures an on-power push; on a tall truck a forward bias can lighten the rear into wheelspin — re-check ride height after.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.58 'Battery Placement' — forward: more steering, less rear traction; p.50 'Weight Distribution': front weight = more steering while accelerating, changes direction slower
CompetitionX RC Tuning Guide — Weight/Battery Position (corroboration: forward bias adds steering, reduces rear traction)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One viscosity step at a time. Mugen: thicker front diff = smoother off-power steering + more on-power steering; too thick makes the rear loose on throttle. On the heavier truggy go conservative — it amplifies the loose-on-throttle side effect.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.2 — Front diff fluid

rules.magnitude_guidance: One viscosity step at a time. Mugen: thinner front diff increases off-power steering and decreases on-power steering; too light makes the car twitchy and hard to drive — a real risk on the high-CG truggy.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.2 — Front diff fluid
Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.19 — Diff Fluid, Front Diff, off-road (corroboration)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One viscosity step at a time. Mugen: thicker center diff = more acceleration, more on-power steering, smoother off-power steering. Heavier center fluid also calms the heavier truggy's on-throttle behaviour.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.2-3 — Center diff fluid

rules.magnitude_guidance: One viscosity step at a time. Mugen: thinner center diff increases on-power traction but decreases acceleration and increases off-power steering. Good for finding bite on a slick, bumpy truggy track.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.2 — Center diff fluid

rules.magnitude_guidance: One viscosity step at a time. Mugen: thicker rear diff = slightly more off-power steering, smoother mid-corner steering, more rear traction on throttle. A stability-friendly first move for a truggy that's loose on power.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.3 — Rear diff fluid
Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.21 — Diff Fluid, Rear Diff, off-road (corroboration)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One viscosity step at a time. Mugen: thinner rear diff gives more mid-corner rotation and makes the rear looser on throttle. Use sparingly on a truggy — it trades away the stability the heavy chassis wants.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.3 — Rear diff fluid

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~25-50 cSt) at a time. Mugen: thicker oil = less overall traction, less responsive on direction changes, but EASIER to drive on high-bite/smooth tracks — exactly what a nervous high-CG truggy needs. Go thicker when it gets hot.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.3 — Shock oil

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~25-50 cSt) at a time. Mugen: lighter shock oil increases traction and is better in the bumps, more responsive. Mugen: when it gets cold outside, go lighter. Watch for added nervousness on the tall truggy.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.3 — Shock oil

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~25-50 cSt) at a time. Mugen: thicker oil is easier to drive on high-bite/smooth tracks; go thicker when hot. On the heavy truggy thicker rear oil flattens the chassis and resists the traction-roll its high CG invites.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.3 — Shock oil

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step (~25-50 cSt) at a time. Mugen: lighter oil = more overall traction, better in bumps. Mugen: when cold, go lighter. Helps a truggy find forward bite on a rough, low-grip surface.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.3 — Shock oil

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate at a time, matched left/right. Mugen: stiffer front springs support the front better and reduce steering; on high-grip tracks stiffer front+rear gives more corner speed and stability — the heavy truggy benefits from the extra support.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.3-4 — Springs

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate at a time, matched left/right. Mugen: softer front springs roll more and increase steering; on low-grip tracks softer springs front and rear increase overall grip and improve bump handling. On a truggy, too soft invites traction roll — step gently.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.3-4 — Springs
Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.41 — Shock Springs (corroboration: softer gives more traction, best for small bumps)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate at a time, matched left/right. Mugen: stiffer rear springs add support but decrease rear traction on corner exit; on high-grip tracks they add stability. Useful to settle a truggy that hooks and rolls on a high-bite exit.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.3-4 — Springs

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring rate at a time, matched left/right. Mugen: softer rear springs give more initial grip and forward traction; on low-grip tracks softer front+rear increases overall grip. On the heavy truggy too soft will roll — pair with adequate ride height.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.3-4 — Springs
Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.41 — Shock Springs (corroboration: softer is great on rear for off-road, gives more traction)

rules.magnitude_guidance: Change one piston step (hole count/size), front pair matched, and re-tune oil. Mugen: more pack / smaller holes need lighter oil, give slower weight transfer, less responsiveness, and land large jumps better — valuable for a heavy truggy off big jumps.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.4 — Pistons

rules.magnitude_guidance: Change one piston step, rear pair matched, and re-tune oil. Mugen: less pack / larger holes need heavier oil, give more weight transfer, more traction, more responsiveness, and absorb bumps better. Helps a truggy hook up on a rough, low-grip surface.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.4 — Pistons

rules.magnitude_guidance: One hole at a time, both sides. Mugen: moving the shocks OUT on the tower makes the car more responsive, jumps better, and is better on technical tracks. On a truggy use the responsiveness deliberately — it can sharpen an already-tall chassis.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.4 — Shock location

rules.magnitude_guidance: One hole at a time, both sides. Mugen: moving the shocks IN on the tower gives softer initial damping, less responsiveness, and is more forgiving — a good calming move for a nervous truggy on a rough track.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.4 — Shock location

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5-1mm at a time via shock collar/preload. AE: lower front ride height creates more push and less chance of flipping in corners. Lowering CG is the single most effective anti-traction-roll lever on a tall truggy — but don't go so low it bottoms.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.29 — Ride Height, front
Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.8 — Ride Height

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5-1mm at a time via shock collar/preload. AE: higher rear ride height gives better acceleration in loose terrain and better lift off jumps. Mugen baseline: run the front 1-2mm LOWER than the rear. Raising the heavy truggy's CG hurts stability — use only to clear rough ground/jumps.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.30 — Ride Height, rear
Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.8 — Ride Height

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1mm of travel at a time, measured on the car (Mugen: top-mount centre to bottom-screw centre), identical left/right. Mugen: more front travel increases on-power steering; more travel front and rear lands better and is easier to drive on rough tracks. Too much can traction-roll on bumpy/rutted mid-corners — a real truggy risk.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.5-6 — Rebound stop (travel)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 1mm of travel at a time, identical left/right. Mugen: more rear travel increases off-power steering; too much travel causes traction roll on bumpy/rutted mid-corners, and less travel slides over small bumps. Reducing rear travel calms a truggy that traction-rolls into ruts.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.5-6 — Rebound stop (travel)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One bar size (~0.1mm wire) at a time. Mugen: thicker front sway bar decreases off-power steering, smooths steering entering the turn, and increases on-power steering; thicker bars are more stable on high-speed/high-traction tracks. A core lever to tame the heavy truggy's chassis roll.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.6 — Sway Bars
Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.7 — Anti-roll Bars, Sway Bars (corroboration: thicker bars for high-traction, more responsive + more stable)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One bar size (~0.1mm wire) at a time. Mugen: thinner front sway bar increases off-power steering and reduces on-power steering. AE: softer/thinner bars suit low and medium bite. Frees up a pushing truggy on a low-grip track without going to a soft spring.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.6 — Sway Bars
Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.7 — Anti-roll Bars, Sway Bars (corroboration: softer/thinner bars for low and medium bite)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One bar size (~0.1mm wire) at a time. Mugen: thicker rear sway bar increases stability in the middle of the turn and increases on-power steering; thicker bars are more stable on high-speed/high-traction tracks. The first reach-for lever against truggy mid-corner traction roll.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.6 — Sway Bars
Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.7 — Anti-roll Bars, Sway Bars (corroboration: thicker bars minimize chassis roll, more stable)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One bar size (~0.1mm wire) at a time. Mugen: thinner rear sway bar increases rear traction and decreases on-power steering. Recovers forward bite for a truggy struggling for drive on a slick surface — at the cost of some mid-corner stability.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.6 — Sway Bars

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.25-0.5 deg at a time, matched left/right; tyres should still wear flat. Mugen: more negative front camber has less steering and is smoother in bumps. A mild calming move for a darty truggy on a rough section.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.6 — Camber

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.25-0.5 deg at a time, matched left/right. Mugen: less negative front camber has more steering. Small, low-cost steering gain for a pushing truggy.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.6 — Camber
Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.12 — Camber, front (corroboration)

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.25-0.5 deg at a time, matched left/right. Mugen: more negative rear camber has less forward traction, more on-power steering, and is better in bumps. Helps a truggy that traction-rolls on a high-bite mid-corner; watch the forward-bite trade-off.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.6 — Camber

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.25-0.5 deg at a time, matched left/right. Mugen: less negative rear camber gives more forward traction but CAN cause the vehicle to traction roll — a sharp warning on a high-CG truggy. Don't chase bite this way on high grip.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.6 — Camber

rules.magnitude_guidance: One hub offset step (+1 or +2mm) per side at a time, symmetric. Mugen: +1/+2mm hubs have slightly less initial grip but increase stability on higher-grip tracks. Widening the heavy truggy's stance is a strong anti-roll lever on high bite.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.7 — Track width

rules.magnitude_guidance: One hub offset step per side at a time, symmetric. Mugen: standard wheel hubs work best on low-grip and dusty conditions (more initial grip). Narrowing recovers grip on a slick, dusty truggy track but gives up stability — step carefully on the tall chassis.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.7 — Track width

rules.magnitude_guidance: Move one shim at a time, both sides. Mugen: longer wheelbase decreases off-power steering but is MORE STABLE, better in bumps, and has more on-power steering. The classic settle-the-truggy move for a fast, rough, open track.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.7 — Wheel Base

rules.magnitude_guidance: Move one shim at a time, both sides. Mugen: shorter wheelbase increases on-power traction and off-power steering, and is better on tight or slick tracks. Sharpens a sluggish truggy on a tight course — but costs the stability the long base provides.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.7 — Wheel Base

rules.magnitude_guidance: One shim/holder step at a time, both sides. Mugen: more anti-squat gives more on-power support, more forward traction, and jumps better. AE: more anti-squat = less side traction, more rear lift in jumps. Strong on-power stability lever for the heavy truggy on smooth high grip.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.7 — Anti squat
Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.8 — Anti-squat, off-road (corroboration)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One shim/holder step at a time, both sides. Mugen: less anti-squat = less off-power steering and less on-power support. AE: less anti-squat = more side traction in corners, more rear traction for slick or bumpy surfaces. Helps a truggy that loses the rear over bumps.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.7 — Anti squat
Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.8 — Anti-squat, off-road (corroboration)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One bushing/insert step, both sides. Mugen: more kick gives more steering entering the turn, more forward traction, and is better in bumps. AE: more kickup turns into the corner more, standard for most situations. A forgiving setting for a truggy on rough, low-grip ground.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.5 — Lower front arm position (kick)
Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.27 — Kickup (corroboration)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One bushing/insert step, both sides. Mugen: less kick decreases off-power steering and increases on-power steering, but is less forgiving in bumps. AE: less kickup = better turn-in through a corner, fast weight transfer to the front, best for high-traction tracks. Use on a smooth high-bite truggy track only.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.5 — Lower front arm position (kick)
Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.27 — Kickup (corroboration)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One arm/link position at a time; re-check camber after. Mugen: a lower front roll centre has more overall grip and steering. Wakes up a pushing truggy on low grip — but a lower roll centre on high bite can over-rotate the tall chassis.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.5 — Lower front arm position (roll centre)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One arm/link position at a time; re-check camber after. Mugen: a higher front roll centre has more support and less overall steering. A stability lever for a truggy that traction-rolls or is too darty into high-bite corners.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.5 — Lower front arm position (roll centre)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One link/hole position at a time; re-check rear camber after. Mugen: a longer rear camber link gives less roll and improves stability and traction. A direct anti-roll lever for the high-CG truggy on high bite.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.7 — Rear Camber Links

rules.magnitude_guidance: One link/hole position at a time; re-check rear camber after. Mugen: a shorter rear camber link gives more roll, increases steering, and handles bumps better. Frees up a pushing truggy on a rough low-grip track — but more roll is risky on the tall chassis at high bite.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.7 — Rear Camber Links

rules.magnitude_guidance: One hole at a time; re-check front toe after. Mugen: ackerman forward is more responsive initially and then smoother on corner exit. Adds turn-in for a lazy truggy on a tight course.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.4 — Ackerman

rules.magnitude_guidance: One hole at a time; re-check front toe after. Mugen: ackerman back has smoother off-power steering and increases on-power steering. Calms an over-darty truggy on a fast, high-grip layout.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.4 — Ackerman

rules.magnitude_guidance: Small bias steps from a 50/50 baseline (Mugen). Mugen: if the vehicle is too aggressive under braking, increase front brake (or decrease rear). More front brake settles a heavy truggy that swaps or over-rotates on entry.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.2 — Brake bias

rules.magnitude_guidance: Small bias steps from a 50/50 baseline (Mugen). Mugen: if the vehicle feels too lazy entering the turn and you want more rotation, decrease front brake or increase rear brake strength. Use sparingly on a truggy — too much rear brake makes the tall chassis unstable on entry.
sources: Mugen MSR Off-Road Tuning Guide (MSR tuning guide.pdf) p.2 — Brake bias

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wing-shim step at a time. AE: a steeper wing angle gives more rear traction. A bolt-on stability lever for a loose, fast truggy — the bigger truggy wing makes this especially effective at speed.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.52 — Wing

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wing-shim step at a time. AE: a more horizontal wing is standard traction (less rear downforce) and frees the rear. Use only if a truggy is glued at the rear and pushing — flattening costs the stability the tall chassis usually wants.
sources: Team Associated RC Cheat Sheets (RC_CheatSheets.pdf) p.52 — Wing

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wire step (0.1mm), e.g. 2.3 → 2.2mm.
sources: HUDY Off-Road Set-Up Book p.32 §1.13

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wire step (0.1mm), e.g. 2.3 → 2.4mm.
sources: HUDY Off-Road Set-Up Book p.32 §1.13

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wire step (0.1mm), e.g. 2.8 → 2.7mm.
sources: HUDY Off-Road Set-Up Book p.32 §1.13

rules.magnitude_guidance: One wire step (0.1mm), e.g. 2.8 → 2.9mm. May cause oversteer.
sources: HUDY Off-Road Set-Up Book p.32 §1.13

rules.magnitude_guidance: One mounting position or add shims behind the wing posts.
sources: HUDY Off-Road Set-Up Book p.33 §1.14

rules.magnitude_guidance: One mounting position.
sources: HUDY Off-Road Set-Up Book p.33 §1.14

rules.magnitude_guidance: One angle position step.
sources: HUDY Off-Road Set-Up Book p.33 §1.14

rules.magnitude_guidance: One angle position step; flattens the car over jumps.
sources: HUDY Off-Road Set-Up Book p.33 §1.14

rules.magnitude_guidance: One mounting position.
sources: HUDY Off-Road Set-Up Book p.33 §1.14

rules.magnitude_guidance: One mounting position.
sources: HUDY Off-Road Set-Up Book p.33 §1.14

rules.magnitude_guidance: One step at a time (e.g. 7000 → 5000 cSt). Too thin makes steering inconsistent and loses forward traction out of corners.

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step thicker (e.g. 500 → 550 cSt), both fronts identical, keeping the front/rear oil offset. Silicone shock oil thins as it heats, so a hot track leaves the baseline under-damped — bouncy, packs less, bottoms on landings; thicker restores the intended damping. Thicken for the MAIN event's temperature, not a hot qualifier: if it cools by the final, over-thick oil goes wooden and loses grip.
sources: JQRacing — THE Guide (Joern Neumann, 1/8 buggy), Set-up Advice: hot weather calls for thicker shock oil
RC Car Stars — The Effects of Temperature on Silicone Shock Oil (~50 cSt / 2.5wt per 10° change)
EuroRC — Basic Shock Oil Setup (silicone oil thins in heat)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step thinner (e.g. 500 → 450 cSt), both fronts identical, keeping the front/rear offset — roughly ~50 cSt per 10° below your baseline temp. Silicone shock oil thickens as it cools, so a cold track leaves the baseline over-damped — harsh, low grip, slow to take a set; thinner restores the intended damping and mechanical grip in the cold.
sources: RC Car Stars — The Effects of Temperature on Silicone Shock Oil (cold thickens silicone; run lighter, ~50 cSt / 2.5wt per 10°)
The RC Racer — Racing on Low Grip / cold conditions: softer, thinner shock oil
EuroRC — Basic Shock Oil Setup (temperature ↔ viscosity)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step thinner on the rear (e.g. 450 → 400 cSt). Same cold-thickening mechanism as the front; thinner rear restores forward bite and compliance lost to over-damping in the cold.
sources: RC Car Stars — The Effects of Temperature on Silicone Shock Oil (cold thickens silicone)
HUDY Off-Road Set-Up Book p.26 §1.9.1 — softer rear shock oil = more rear traction / compliance
EuroRC — Basic Shock Oil Setup (temperature ↔ viscosity)

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step thinner on the fronts (e.g. 500 → 450 cSt), both identical, keeping the front/rear offset. On a wet or standing-water surface, thinner oil lets the suspension react fast enough for the tyre to punch THROUGH the water film to the track beneath and keep the limited grip working — too-thick oil skates the tyre across the surface. If the track is wet AND cold this is the SAME change as the cold step: make it once, not twice.
sources: Hearns Hobbies — RC Shock Setup Guide for Different Track Conditions (Wet: thinner oil so tyres cut through the surface water)
JQRacing — THE Guide (Joern Neumann, 1/8 buggy): on slippery, bumpy tracks thinner oils are better
The RC Racer — Racing on Low Grip: softer, thinner shock oil

rules.magnitude_guidance: One oil step thinner on the rear (e.g. 450 → 400 cSt). Same water-film mechanism as the front: thinner rear oil reacts fast enough to cut through the wet surface for forward bite and compliance. Mind the rear — do not also thin the rear DIFF for wet (that is a deferred, conditional change); one lever at a time. Wet AND cold is the same single step.
sources: Hearns Hobbies — RC Shock Setup Guide for Different Track Conditions (Wet: thinner oil so tyres cut through the surface water)
JQRacing — THE Guide (Joern Neumann, 1/8 buggy): on slippery, bumpy tracks thinner oils are better
The RC Racer — Racing on Low Grip: softer, thinner shock oil
